component.name: Notav
component.summary: Notes and a journal kept in your Nextcloud

description.p: Notav keeps your notes as plain Markdown files in your Nextcloud, so the Nextcloud Notes app and Obsidian can open the same folder.

ul.li: Works offline; changes sync when the server is reachable
Notes edited on two devices at once are both kept
Folders, search, and a Markdown editor
Connects through GNOME Online Accounts or a browser sign-in, to more than one account
Or keeps your notes on this device only, without a server

Accounts, as in Todav: notes of more than one Nextcloud account, and On This Device Only, notes kept on this computer without a server. The welcome page offers a GNOME Online Accounts account, a Nextcloud server or this device; Preferences → Accounts adds more, each with its page (use it or not, its name, signing in again, its server, notes folder and status, Remove). With more than one shown, each account is a row of the tree with its notes under it
A dense tree in Preferences: smaller rows, as in Files
Favorites, shared with Nextcloud Files and the Nextcloud Notes app: "Add to Favorites" in a note's menu stars it; starred notes come first in their folder, with a star

Trash in the main menu: the notes and folders deleted from the notes folder that Nextcloud's trash bin keeps, to restore or delete for good; only where the server has a trash bin, and deleting for good only where it allows that
Versions in a note's menu: the earlier versions Nextcloud keeps of it, each to look at and restore (an edit Ctrl+Z undoes); only where the server keeps versions
When Notav is updated while it runs, a banner offers Restart into the new version (as in Todav)
Folders in the tree show how many notes they hold, their folders' included, dimmed
An outline of the open note's headings at its right, shown and hidden with the Outline button; a click goes to the heading
Note icons in the tree, set in Preferences: on notes only (the default), on folders too, or none
Rename and delete folders from the sidebar menu; a note changed on another device meanwhile is kept, and its folder with it
Undo for deleted, moved and renamed notes and folders: the Undo button on the toast, or Ctrl+Z

Editor mode, the new default: every part of GitHub Flavored Markdown styled as it is meant (headings, emphasis, code, quotes, lists and tasks, tables in columns, links and bare URLs, footnotes, front matter), the Markdown marks dimmed. Source mode keeps the editor as it was; the two toggles at the header's right switch between them

A view menu next to them: the text's size (also Ctrl+plus, Ctrl+minus, Ctrl+0) and Full Width, the text across the window but for a small margin, and Wrap Lines (on by default; off, long lines scroll sideways); kept on each device
Each mode's font in Preferences, under Editor, for each device: Source mode's is monospace (the system's by default, and only monospace ones are offered)
In Editor mode, a click on a task's [ ] or [x] ticks or unticks it
In Editor mode, Enter in a list starts the next item: the same bullet, the next number (the numbers below moved up), an open task after a task; Enter on an empty item ends the list
In Editor mode, Ctrl+click opens a link, an autolink or a bare URL; Alt+Enter the one at the cursor

Links between notes: a Markdown link to a note (text, ../Folder/Note.md) or a wiki link ([[Note]], [[Folder/Note|shown]], by title or path, as in Obsidian) opens the note, at the heading after a #; a note a link names that is not there yet is made
Backlinks: under a note, the notes that link to it, each opened with a click

Journal: Today's Note in the header (Ctrl+T) opens the day's note, made from a template note if there is none (its {{title}} and {{date}} filled in); its folder, template and name format (YYYY-MM-DD by default, / for folders) are set on a Journal page in Preferences, the folder and template fields suggesting what there is

Tables in Editor mode: kept aligned (the pipes lined up, the alignment in the |---| row) once the cursor leaves a changed row; from the right-click menu, insert a table, add, move, duplicate and delete rows and columns, align a column or sort by it; rows copied from a spreadsheet are pasted as a table

Table handles in Editor mode, as in Obsidian: over a table, a grip in the column (on the |---| row) and on the row's left edge opens its menu or, dragged, moves it; bars past the last column and under the last row add one

Tables from the keyboard in Editor mode: Enter after a header line (| Name | Size |) makes it a table with an empty row; in a table, Tab and Shift+Tab go from cell to cell and Enter to the next row, past the last one adding a row, and Enter on an empty last row leaves the table; text typed in a cell takes the place of its padding, so the pipes stay in line
An Editor page in Preferences for what Editor mode does by itself: "Format tables", under Markdown, turns off the tables' tidying as the cursor leaves a row (Format Table in the menu still works)
Deleting a note no longer asks first: the toast can undo it
The notes folder is set on its account's page in Preferences, on each device; the one of the account settings sync through is offered to other devices signing in to it
Settings sync through the account chosen in "Sync settings with" (Preferences → Accounts), or stay on this device; Remove Account takes the place of Sign Out
An older Notav no longer opens data a newer one left (after a downgrade, say): it shows a window saying to update, and leaves the data as it is
Sync stopping with "UNIQUE constraint failed: notes.fileid" after a note was moved and a new one took its old name before the next sync, and the new note not showing on other devices
A folder moved before signing out or into another account, and not synced yet, no longer moves a folder of that name in the next account's files
Screen readers name the notes in the sidebar, not only the folders
Clicking into a long note no longer scrolls it to its end; the note follows the cursor, and Page Up and Page Down move by a screen, not to the start or the end
Notes kept as Markdown files in a folder of your Nextcloud Files (Notes/ by default, as the Nextcloud Notes app), synced over WebDAV; Notav works from a local copy, also offline
Sign-in through GNOME Online Accounts, the browser, or a login name and app password, then the notes folder to use
The notes folder as a tree of folders and notes in the sidebar, as in Obsidian
Search through titles and text, ignoring case and accents
Markdown editor that saves as you type, styled for reading: headings sized by level, the Markdown marks dimmed, a line of about 80 characters; the title renames the note
Drag notes and folders into and out of folders in the sidebar
Sidebar menu (right click): new note or folder inside a folder, next to a note, or at the top level; delete a note
A note changed on two devices at once keeps both versions: yours as a conflict copy next to it
A note locked on the server (open in Nextcloud Text) waits with its change and the rest syncs; the app says who locked it and since when, and can unlock it
Preferences: style, notes folder (moving the notes there or not), account, settings sync
Settings synced between devices through .config/notav/settings.json
Polish translation
About has a Support page with where to support Notav's development: Ko-fi, GitHub Sponsors and Liberapay
An RPM spec for Fedora, built on COPR from .copr/Makefile; Notav uses the system's SQLite
